origin: OWASP/railsgoat (official, ALIVE — case-sensitive lowercase name; default branch main)
supersedes: the 2018 mirror seal (smDahlgren/RailGoat @ f1de24f — suspended BLOCKED 2026-11-12; that training commit does NOT exist in official history)
reference_source: spec/vulnerabilities/*.rb on the official main — one official failing Capybara spec per vulnerability

classification.label: broken_auth_spec.rb
classification.reason: credential enumeration on the unauthenticated login form (sessions#new is root; error text distinguishes unknown-email vs wrong-password)
classification.evidence_f5951f1: app/models/user.rb:41-48 authenticate() raises "#{email} doesn't exist!" vs "Incorrect Password!" — the sessions#create flash echoes e.message; both spec scenarios drive ONLY /login unauthenticated

classification.label: command_injection_spec.rb
classification.reason: upload-form filename injection requires an AUTHENTICATED session (benefit_forms has no authenticated skip) — not reachable by an unauthenticated crawl
classification.evidence_f5951f1: app/controllers/benefit_forms_controller.rb has ZERO skip_before_action (authenticated enforced); Benefits.make_backup (app/models/benefits.rb:15) runs system("cp #{full_file_name} ...") with the attacker filename — vulnerable code, but behind the auth gate on f5951f1

classification.label: csrf_spec.rb
classification.reason: CSRF spec drives an authenticated victim session

classification.label: insecure_dor_spec.rb
classification.reason: both DOR scenarios operate on /users/:id/benefit_forms and /users/:id/work_info — authenticated surfaces on f5951f1
classification.evidence_f5951f1: benefit_forms_controller.rb and work_info_controller.rb have ZERO skip_before_action :authenticated — attack one (download param name=config/database.yml) and attack two (cross-user work_info read) both login(normal_user) first in the spec itself

classification.label: mass_assignment_spec.rb
classification.reason: attack two posts admin:"t" to /users (signup) — an UNAUTHENTICATED POST surface; permit! mass-assignment is observable there
classification.evidence_f5951f1: app/controllers/users_controller.rb:5 skip_before_action :authenticated, only: [:new, :create] + user_params (lines 49-51) params.require(:user).permit! — the signup create path accepts the admin field unauthenticated (spec attack two does page.driver.post "/users" with NO login)

classification.label: password_complexity_spec.rb
classification.reason: policy weakness, not an HTTP-response-observable class
classification.evidence_f5951f1: unchanged nature (no password policy on signup; not an HTTP response class)

classification.label: password_hashing_spec.rb
classification.reason: weak hashing in DB — not an HTTP response class

classification.label: sensitive_data_exposure.rb
classification.reason: SSN cleartext is served on /users/:id/work_info — an authenticated surface on f5951f1
classification.evidence_f5951f1: work_info_controller.rb has ZERO skip_before_action :authenticated; spec line 18 login(normal_user) before visiting work_info; encrypt_ssn stays commented out (app/models/work_info.rb:5) — vulnerable code, but behind the auth gate

classification.label: sql_injection_spec.rb
classification.reason: the SQLi surface (User.where on hidden user_id) is users#update — an authenticated surface on f5951f1
classification.evidence_f5951f1: app/controllers/users_controller.rb:29 User.where("id = '#{params[:user][:id]}'") — update is NOT in the [:new, :create] authenticated skip; spec drives it via account_settings AFTER login(normal_user). The login form itself uses find_by_email (no injection) — no unauthenticated SQLi surface remains

classification.label: unvalidated_redirects_spec.rb
classification.reason: redirect parameter is observed on the unauthenticated root/login flow
classification.evidence_f5951f1: app/controllers/sessions_controller.rb:7 @url = params[:url] (sessions#new = root, unauthenticated) and line 12 path = params[:url].present? ? params[:url] : home_dashboard_index_path — the url parameter flows from the unauthenticated login POST into redirect_to (spec starts with visit "/?url=http://example.com/do/evil/things" BEFORE any login)

classification.label: url_access_spec.rb
classification.reason: admin/1/dashboard is guarded by the application-wide authenticated before_action (plus administrative) on f5951f1 — the unauthenticated probe is redirected to login, so no admin content is observable without a session
classification.evidence_f5951f1: admin_controller.rb:3 before_action :administrative, if: :admin_param — and the APPLICATION-WIDE before_action :authenticated (application_controller.rb:3) with NO skip in admin_controller: unauthenticated GET /admin/1/dashboard is redirected to root; the vulnerability (non-admin user reaching the admin dashboard) requires login(normal_user) per the spec itself

classification.label: xss_spec.rb
classification.reason: reflected XSS lives on the account_settings update form — an authenticated surface on f5951f1
classification.evidence_f5951f1: xss_spec.rb:16 login(normal_user) then visit account_settings; the injection (First name field -> users#update) is behind the auth gate

notes: RECLASSIFICATION DIFFERENCE vs the 2018 seal (9 measurable -> 3): on official main f5951f1, ApplicationController enforces before_action :authenticated on every controller except sessions(new/create), users(new/create), password_resets, api/v1 (http-token gate) and tutorials — so command_injection, insecure_dor, sensitive_data_exposure, sql_injection, url_access and xss now sit behind the auth gate. Per the SEALED criteria (measurable = URL reachable by an UNAUTHENTICATED crawl), those six labels move to out_of_scope. This is the sealed criteria applied faithfully to the new commit, NOT a capability-driven reclassification (no engine limitation is involved — the labels' reachability changed on the new commit itself).
per the two-number rule (SPEC §3.2.1) any future re-enable of engine authentication may move these labels back to measurable via a NEW seal commit documenting before/after numbers
Dockerfile on f5951f1 builds FROM ruby:3.4.1 official with zero bring-up patches; Gemfile.lock bundler 4.0.4; README rails db:setup standard — no archive mirrors needed
step-zero bring-up must use the official repo OWASP/railsgoat @ f5951f1 (NOT the smDahlgren mirror @ f1de24f which is syntax-broken and fixes sealed vulns)
